title: LAMBDA is lexically scoped, does not force unused error arguments, returns #CALC! uncalled, and rejects duplicate parameters at entry
statement: In Excel 16.0.20527, LAMBDA([parameter1, ...], calculation) uses lexical scoping over captured outer bindings (=LET(xx,1,fn,LAMBDA(xx),LET(xx,2,fn())) -> 1), does not raise an unused argument's error (=LAMBDA(xx,7)(1/0) -> 7), returns #VALUE! when called with too few required or too many arguments, and yields #CALC! when an uncalled LAMBDA value reaches a cell (directly or via IFS/SWITCH/HSTACK). At formula entry (0x800A03EC), Excel refuses empty LAMBDA() and duplicate case-folded parameter names (=LAMBDA(xx,XX,xx)(1,2)), while allowing postfix calls after IF, CHOOSE, SWITCH, IFS, and LET but refusing postfix calls after IFERROR, IFNA, or MAP.
basis: Measured in Excel 16.0.20527.20088 across fn2_questions (fn2_q017-020, fn2_q098-104, fn2_q110-120), f3_arrays (rows 33-44), and entry measurements in excel-entry.tsv (dc-mx3x).
